claim: CAPO proves that GRPO-style overconfidence -- where incorrect responses obtain lower perplexity than correct ones -- stems specifically from uncertainty-agnostic advantage estimation, which misaligns optimization gradients with an AUC-style discrimination objective.
stance_target: standard GRPO advantage estimation is compatible with good discrimination (AUC/AUROC)
quoted_support: We first prove that this degradation in GRPO-style algorithms stems from their uncertainty-agnostic advantage estimation, which inevitably misaligns optimization gradients with calibration.

claim: CAPO replaces the standard advantage estimator with a logistic AUC surrogate loss that is theoretically consistent and admits a provable regret bound, making advantage estimation uncertainty-aware and directly optimizing for discrimination rather than calibration error alone.
stance_target: a discrimination-first (AUC-surrogate) training objective is a viable alternative to calibration-error-first objectives like Brier/log-scoring
quoted_support: It adopts a logistic AUC surrogate loss that is theoretically consistent and admits regret bound, enabling uncertainty-aware advantage estimation.

claim: CAPO-1.5B improves calibration by up to 15% while matching or beating GRPO accuracy on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks, and boosts downstream inference-time-scaling accuracy by up to 5%; under an abstention option it achieves a Pareto-optimal precision-coverage trade-off.
stance_target: AUC-surrogate calibration-aware policy optimization achieves both calibration and accuracy gains, plus downstream abstention utility, at small model scale
scope_conditions: CAPO-1.5B, mathematical reasoning benchmarks, inference-time scaling and abstention settings
quoted_support: Experiments on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks show that CAPO-1.5B significantly improves calibration by up to 15% while achieving accuracy comparable to or better than GRPO, and further boosts accuracy on downstream inference-time scaling tasks by up to 5%.
